title: My monthly budget

prepTasks.word: At the end of the month,

writingModel: Managing money as a university student is one of the most important skills I am learning at WKU. Before I came to Uralsk, I never thought carefully about budgets or expenses. My parents paid for everything, and I did not think about prices. But when I arrived here alone, with a fixed amount of money each month, I had to learn quickly. Now, after one year, I have a clear system — and I am proud of it.

Every month, my total income is twenty-five thousand tenge. Fifteen thousand comes from my parents as a monthly allowance — they send it on the first of every month, always on time. The remaining ten thousand I earn myself through a tutoring job: I help two younger students from my faculty with Economics once a week, and they each pay me five thousand tenge per month. Having my own income makes me feel more independent and more careful about how I spend money.

My fixed expenses take up the largest part of my budget. The dormitory costs eight thousand tenge per month — that is my biggest single expense. My mobile phone plan is one thousand five hundred tenge, which gives me unlimited calls within Kazakhstan and four gigabytes of internet data. Transport — mainly buses to the city centre and back — costs around two thousand tenge. So my fixed expenses total eleven thousand five hundred tenge per month. These costs do not change, so I always know exactly what I need to cover first.

After fixed expenses, I spend approximately seven thousand tenge on food each month. About four thousand five hundred goes to the WKU cafeteria — I eat breakfast there almost every morning and lunch on weekdays. The remaining two thousand five hundred goes on fruit, snacks, and occasional café visits with friends. I also set aside two thousand tenge for study materials — books, notebooks, pens, and printing fees. For personal spending and small pleasures — a film, a magazine, a gift for a friend — I allow myself no more than two thousand tenge per month. That is a firm rule I follow carefully.

At the end of each month, I try to save two thousand five hundred tenge. I keep my savings in a separate digital account so I am not tempted to spend them. My goal is to save thirty thousand tenge by the end of the academic year — enough to buy a good laptop to replace my old, slow one. This budget plan is not always easy to follow. Some months, an unexpected expense appears — a medical visit, a new textbook, a birthday gift. But having a plan means I always know where I stand. Managing money well is, I believe, as important as any subject at university.

writingPhrases.category: Talking about income — how much you receive
items: My monthly income is [amount] tenge.
Every month, I receive [amount] tenge from [source].
I earn [amount] tenge per month by [doing something].
My parents send me [amount] tenge on the [date] of every month.
I also earn [amount] tenge from my part-time [job].
My total income comes from [source 1] and [source 2].

writingPhrases.category: Describing expenses — what you spend money on
items: My biggest expense is [item], which costs [amount] tenge.
I spend about [amount] tenge on [category] every month.
Fixed expenses: [item 1] ([amount]) + [item 2] ([amount]) = [total].
For food, I spend approximately [amount] tenge per month.
I set aside [amount] tenge for [books / transport / personal spending].
I allow myself no more than [amount] tenge on [entertainment / going out].

writingPhrases.category: Comparing and budgeting — more / less / the same
items: This month I spent more / less than last month on [category].
[Item A] is more expensive than [Item B] — [amount] vs [amount].
Compared to [last month / last year], I spend [more / less] on...
My fixed costs are [amount] tenge. My flexible costs are about [amount].
In total, my expenses come to [amount] tenge per month.
That leaves [amount] tenge at the end of the month.

writingPhrases.category: Savings and goals — your financial plans
items: I try to save [amount] tenge every month.
My goal is to save [total amount] by [date / end of year].
I keep my savings in a [separate account / envelope / digital wallet].
I am saving for [a laptop / a trip / an emergency fund / a gift].
Managing money well is one of the most important skills at university.
Having a budget means I always know where I stand financially.
